title: User guide
intro: Step-by-step flows for each kind of user. Every element you meet is listed with the way it is meant to be located, so you can practise each locator style on purpose.

gettingStarted.title: Getting started
steps: Start everything with npm run start:all (Windows: npm run start:all:win) and open https://localhost:3001. Accept the self-signed certificate once.
For known passwords, run npm run seed -- --reset-passwords --demo. Every demo user then signs in with Namma-Bengaluru-2026.
Codes and notices the app sends (SMS and e-mail) appear in the dev inbox at /dev/inbox.
Add ?hints=1 to any URL to show which locator style each practice element uses.

visitor.name: Visitor (not signed in)
visitor.intro: Someone without a session: a new joiner, or staff who forgot their password.

teller.name: Teller
teller.intro: Runs the cash counter and their drawer.

everyone.name: Every signed-in user
everyone.intro: Parts of the app every role sees.

cookieConsent.title: Accept or refuse cookies
cookieConsent.summary: The sign-in page is blocked until you answer the cookie banner.
steps: Open /login in a fresh browser profile (or clear site data).
Try to click the Staff ID field: nothing happens, because the page behind the banner is inert.
Click Choose cookies, tick Analytics, and click Save choices. Or click Accept all or Reject non-essential.
Reload the page: the banner doesn't come back. Click Cookie settings (bottom left) to change your answer.
cookieConsent.expected: The banner closes and the sign-in form works. The choice is stored in localStorage as csm.cookieConsent.

requestAccess.title: Request staff access
requestAccess.summary: A new joiner asks for an account; an administrator decides.
steps: On the sign-in page, click New here? Request access.
Click Send request straight away to see every inline error.
Fill in the form. Mobile formats itself as you type (98450 12345); employee numbers look like E10234.
Open the acceptable use policy and privacy notice links: each opens a dialog.
Tick both consent boxes (the training e-mails box is optional) and click Send request.
Send the same form again: it's refused while the first request is pending.
requestAccess.expected: A confirmation with a request number like AR-2026-000003. A receipt e-mail appears in the dev inbox.

forgotPassword.title: Reset a forgotten password
forgotPassword.summary: Staff ID, then a 6-digit code from the dev inbox, then a new password.
steps: On the sign-in page, click Forgot your password? and enter a staff ID such as csr002.
Click Send code. The page says where the code went. It says the same for IDs that don't exist.
Open the dev inbox in another tab and copy the 6-digit code from the newest SMS.
Type a wrong code first: you're told how many attempts are left. Then paste the right code into any box; all six fill in and it checks itself.
Watch Send a new code: it's disabled with a countdown for 30 seconds, and the code expires after 5 minutes.
Choose a new password (at least 12 characters, not a common one) and confirm it. Use the eye button to show it.
forgotPassword.expected: Your password was changed. Sign in with the new password; a locked account is unlocked too. A "password changed" e-mail appears in the dev inbox.

devInbox.title: Read messages in the dev inbox
devInbox.summary: Every SMS and e-mail the practice environment sent.
steps: Open /dev/inbox (or Pages → Dev inbox in the sidebar).
Filter by staff ID (e.g. csr002) and channel.
Leave Refresh every 5 s ticked: new messages appear on their own. Set ?inboxInterval=1000 to refresh faster.
Clear inbox deletes everything, after a confirmation.
devInbox.expected: Newest first. The code is in the Message column of the SMS row.

decideAccessRequest.title: Approve or reject an access request
decideAccessRequest.summary: Administrators turn requests into staff users.
steps: Sign in as admin001 and open Administration → Access → Users & access.
Scroll to Access requests. Two seeded requests are pending.
Click Reject on one, give a reason, and confirm.
Click Approve on the other. Change the suggested staff ID, role or branch if you want, then confirm.
Copy the one-time password from the dialog. Switch Show to Approved to see the decided request.
decideAccessRequest.expected: A new staff user exists; they must choose their own password at first sign-in. The applicant gets an e-mail in the dev inbox.

commandPalette.title: Jump anywhere with the command palette
commandPalette.summary: Ctrl+K (⌘K on a Mac) opens a searchable list of screens and actions.
steps: Press Ctrl+K anywhere, including inside a text field, or click Search in the top bar.
Type part of a screen name (e.g. board) and press Enter.
Open it again and type the number of a customer from your branch (copy one from Customer search), e.g. 124 or CIF-000124, then press Enter to open that customer.
Use ↑/↓ to move, Esc to close. Switch language and Sign out are also listed.
commandPalette.expected: The palette closes and the chosen screen opens. Focus returns to where it was when you press Esc.

sidebar.title: Collapse and expand the menu
sidebar.summary: Menu groups and sub-groups fold away and stay folded.
steps: Click a group heading such as Customers: its links disappear. Click it again to show them.
As admin001, Administration has an Access sub-group. Collapse it on its own.
Reload the page: collapsed groups stay collapsed.
The Pages group holds utility pages such as the dev inbox.
sidebar.expected: Each heading's aria-expanded changes, and links inside a collapsed group are hidden (not just scrolled away).

announcements.title: Read and dismiss announcements
announcements.summary: Notices from administrators across the top of every page.
steps: Sign in as csr001 (MG Road): you see two announcements. csr002 (Jayanagar) sees only the one for all branches.
Dismiss one with ✕. It stays dismissed after a reload.
To see it again, clear csm.dismissedAnnouncements in localStorage.
announcements.expected: The bar shows the most severe notice first. Critical notices have no ✕.

breadcrumbs.title: Go back with breadcrumbs
breadcrumbs.summary: Earlier parts of the breadcrumb are links.
steps: Open Customer search and click any customer to open Customer 360.
In the top bar the breadcrumb reads Customers / Customer search / CIF-…
Click Customer search to go back to the search.
breadcrumbs.expected: Only parts with a page behind them are links; the current page is bold and marked aria-current="page".

onboardKyc.title: Onboard a customer with OCR, photo, e-KYC and signature
onboardKyc.summary: Let the app read the ID card, take the customer's photo, verify them with the e-KYC provider, and capture their signature.
steps: Go to Customers → Onboard customer. Fill Personal details and Contact & address (Next on each), then you are on KYC & documents.
Under Read the ID card, click Choose card image and pick testresources/ocr/id-blurry.png. Highlighted rows were read with low confidence.

Tick Checked against the card on each highlighted row. Rows for the name, date of birth and city compare the card with what you entered; tick Use the card's value to take it. Next stays blocked until every highlighted row is checked.
The ID number from the sample card doesn't match any accepted format: choose an ID type and correct the number (for a PAN, ABCPE1234F).

Under Customer photo, click the camera button (title Start camera) and allow the camera, then Capture. If you refuse the camera, use the upload button (title Upload a photo) with testresources/media/testimage.jpg.

Click Verify with e-KYC. In the provider window, pick an answer under Simulate the registry's answer, tick the consent box and click Verify identity. Try Registry name differs to see the mismatch warning.

Upload at least one ID document, click Next, and on Review & submit have the customer sign in the signature box. Submit stays disabled until there is a signature. Tick both declarations and click Submit.
onboardKyc.expected: Fields read from the card are filled and flagged ones must be checked; the e-KYC result shows a reference (EKYC-…) and any difference from the form; the customer is submitted with a CIF, and Customer 360 shows the photo and "e-KYC verified".

nominees.title: Add nominees
nominees.summary: Record up to three nominees whose shares add up to 100%.
steps: On the Contact & address step, type the mobile number: it is shown as 98450 12345 while only the digits are stored.
Under Nominee, tick Add nominee. A first nominee row appears with a 100% share.
Enter a date of birth under 18 years ago: a Guardian name field appears and is required.
Click Add another nominee and split the shares (for example 60 and 40). The running total shows under the rows.
Click Next. Shares that don't total 100%, or a missing guardian, stop you with a message.
nominees.expected: The nominees are saved with the draft and listed on Review & submit and on Customer 360 (KYC tab).

unsavedChanges.title: Leave a form with unsaved changes
unsavedChanges.summary: The onboarding wizard, the Edit customer panel and New request warn before you lose unsaved work.
steps: Start onboarding a customer and type in any field without saving.
Click another menu item (for example Dashboard). A dialog asks Leave without saving?
Click Stay on this page to keep your work, or Discard changes to leave.
Type again, then reload the browser tab: the browser shows its own Leave site? warning.
On Customer 360, click Edit, change a field and close the panel: the same dialog appears.
unsavedChanges.expected: Nothing is lost unless you choose Discard changes. Saving (Next, Save draft, Save) clears the warning.

customerPhoto.title: See the customer's photo
customerPhoto.summary: Customer 360 shows the customer's photo, or their initials when there is none or it can't be loaded.
steps: Open a customer onboarded with a photo (see Onboard a customer with OCR, photo, e-KYC and signature).
The photo appears next to the name. Customers without a photo show their initials.
To see the fallback for a broken image, block the photo's request in the browser's developer tools and reload.
customerPhoto.expected: The picture is a .c360-photo element; its data-state is loaded, loading or broken.

searchShortcuts.title: Work faster in Customer search
searchShortcuts.summary: Select, open and act on search results with the mouse or keyboard, and preview a customer without leaving the list.
steps: Go to Customers → Customer search and click Search.
Click a row once: it is selected (highlighted) but stays on the list. Double-click it, or press Enter on a selected row, to open Customer 360.
Right-click a row (or press Shift+F10 on it): choose Open, Copy CIF, New service request or Request block. Items you aren't allowed to use stay visible but greyed out with the reason.

Rest the pointer on a CIF for a moment: a card shows the customer's name, status, KYC, risk, branch and masked mobile. The same works on the Request board list view and the approval queue on the Dashboard, and on staff IDs there.
searchShortcuts.expected: Only a double-click or Enter opens the customer; Copy CIF says "Copied" (or explains if the browser blocked it).

customer360Tools.title: Use the Customer 360 tools
customer360Tools.summary: Create a request for a category straight from Customer 360, check an account number the customer reads out, and act on offers.
steps: Open an active customer from Customer search.
Click Actions, then Create request ▸ and pick a category. New request opens with the customer and category filled in.

On Overview, under Accounts, click Copy next to an account number. Then type the number into Confirm account number: it says whether it matches and that it was typed. Paste it instead: it is accepted but marked as pasted.
If an offer banner shows above the customer, click Not now: it stays hidden for this customer for 30 days in this browser.
Hover or click the ⓘ next to KYC and Risk rating (KYC tab) and SLA (Service requests tab) to read how they work.
On a long Activity log, scroll down and use the back-to-top button.
customer360Tools.expected: New request opens pre-filled; the confirmation reports match and typed or pasted; the offer stays hidden after Not now.

creditStanding.title: Check a customer's credit standing
creditStanding.summary: Customer 360 loads the customer's bureau score a little after the page; supervisors also see the full bureau report.
steps: Open an active customer. On Overview, the Credit standing panel first says it is fetching the score, then shows the score on a gauge with its band and date.
Some customers have no bureau record: the panel says so.
To practise the failure case, add ?bureauFail=1 to the address: the panel says Bureau unavailable; click Retry.
Signed in as a supervisor (View PII), wait a little longer: the full bureau report appears in a frame below the panel.
Add ?bureauDelay=0 to remove the waits.
creditStanding.expected: Score 300–900 with band Excellent (750+), Good (700–749), Fair (650–699) or Poor; the same customer always shows the same score.

cookieBanner.name: Blocking cookie banner
cookieBanner.hint: Buttons by text only: //button[normalize-space()='Accept all']. The page behind is inert until you answer.

maskedMobile.name: Masked mobile input
maskedMobile.hint: input[name='mobile']; the raw digits are in data-raw.

termsModal.name: Policy dialogs
termsModal.hint: Open from the links by text; the dialog is role=dialog with the policy title.

forgotForm.name: Forgot-password fields
forgotForm.hint: By label: getByLabel('Staff ID'), getByLabel('New password'). Ids are generated by React and change.

otpBoxes.name: Six-box code input
otpBoxes.hint: Ids like otp-3fa9c1-0 change on every load: input[id^='otp-'], or the group by its label 'Verification code'.

countdown.name: Expiry and resend countdowns
countdown.hint: Text such as 'Send a new code in 0:24'; wait for the button to become enabled.

passwordToggle.name: Show/hide password
passwordToggle.hint: getByRole('button', { name: 'Show' }); aria-pressed reflects the state.

inboxTable.name: Inbox table
inboxTable.hint: No ids or classes on rows: //table/tbody/tr[td[2]='sms'][1]/td[5].

decisionModal.name: Approve/reject dialog
decisionModal.hint: Fields by data-field (staffId, role, branch, note); confirm with button[data-action='confirm-approve'].

palette.name: Command palette
palette.hint: getByRole('dialog', { name: 'Command palette' }) with a combobox and listbox of options.

navGroups.name: Collapsible menu groups
navGroups.hint: getByRole('button', { name: 'Customers' }) with aria-expanded; the sub-group is a nested button.

ocrPanel.name: ID-card OCR results
ocrPanel.hint: [data-qa='ocr-row'][data-field='idNumber']; read data-confidence and data-flagged. The file input is [data-qa='ocr-file'].

cameraCapture.name: Camera photo with upload fallback
cameraCapture.hint: Icon buttons named only by title: button[title='Start camera'], [title='Capture'], [title='Retake']. State is on .camera[data-state].

ekycFrame.name: Cross-origin e-KYC frame
ekycFrame.hint: iframe[title='e-KYC provider'] from https://localhost:4002: switch into the frame first; inside, #ekyc-consent and the Verify identity button.

signaturePad.name: Signature pad
signaturePad.hint: canvas#customer-signature: draw with pointer moves; the wrapper's data-strokes and data-empty show the result.

unsavedDialog.name: Unsaved-changes dialog
unsavedDialog.hint: Find it by text: the Stay on this page and Discard changes buttons.

customerPhoto.name: Customer photo with initials fallback
customerPhoto.hint: .c360-photo; img inside when loaded, initials when broken (data-state).

rowDoubleClick.name: Double-click row
rowDoubleClick.hint: tr[data-row-id='CIF-000124']: dblclick() opens; a single click sets data-selected="true".

rowContextMenu.name: Right-click row menu
rowContextMenu.hint: Right-click the row, then find items by text: getByRole('menuitem', { name: 'Copy CIF' }).

hoverPreview.name: Hover preview card
hoverPreview.hint: Hover [title='Preview CIF-000124'] (or [title='Preview sup001']) for 0.4 s; the card is role=tooltip.

actionsSubmenu.name: Actions menu with submenu
actionsSubmenu.hint: getByRole('button', { name: 'Actions' }), then menuitem 'Create request', then the category menuitem.

offerBanner.name: Offer banner
offerBanner.hint: .promo-banner and its .btn (Not now); data-offer names the offer.

sectionInfoTips.name: Section ⓘ tips
sectionInfoTips.hint: getByRole('button', { name: 'About KYC' }); the explanation appears while hovered or after a click.

backToTop.name: Back-to-top button
backToTop.hint: button[title='Back to top'], shown after scrolling a screen down.

bureauWidget.name: Bureau score web component
bureauWidget.hint: csm-bureau-score has an open shadow root with a nested csm-gauge (two roots to pierce); Retry is slotted from the light DOM.

bureauDelayed.name: Late-loading bureau panel
bureauDelayed.hint: [data-qa='bureau-panel'][data-state='ready'|'none'|'error']: wait for the state, not a fixed time.

bureauReport.name: Late-loading report iframe
bureauReport.hint: iframe[title='Full bureau report'] is added a few seconds after the score; wait for it, then switch into it.
